title: SoftBody3D permanently expands in size after toggling its `process_mode`
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
- Godot v4.8-dev6 (Jolt Physics)
- Godot v4.7.2 (Jolt Physics)
- Godot v4.6.2 (Jolt Physics)

### System information

Fedora Linux 43 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR)

### Issue description

If you make a `SoftBody3D` and the following conditions are met:

- The `SoftBody3D` has a `pressure_coefficient` greater than 0
- The `SoftBody3D`'s `process_mode` is toggled between `Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED` and `Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`

...then it will grow in size permanently every time the `process_mode` is toggled, with seemingly no way to reset it to its original size.

In other words, it keeps expanding:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08523650-d55f-4a22-ae42-3e1a820f018d

As you can see, it keeps getting bigger. I would expect the soft body to stay the same size.

Potentially related issues:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56142 (but that was back in 2021, before Jolt Physics was integrated)
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3535

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce it, you can just run the reproduction project included below. It will automatically start toggling the `process_mode` and you should see the `SoftBody3D` expanding.

(Note: in Godot 4.6.x and below, you need to set the `SoftBody3D`'s mass to 0kg and set the pressure to about ~4000, else it will explode. [This is because the weight calculation changed between those two versions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116041). The expanding bug is still present in both versions though.)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[soft_body_bug_MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32440544/soft_body_bug_MRP.zip)
